definitions.explanation: The gradual buildup or accumulation of something over time, whether tangible (wealth, fat, substances) or intangible (knowledge, experience, stress).

examples.japanese: {疲労|ひろう}が{蓄積|ちくせき}している。
{長年|ながねん}の{経験|けいけん}の{蓄積|ちくせき}が{彼|かれ}の{強|つよ}みだ。
examples.english: The accumulation of many years of experience is his strength.

examples.japanese: {毎日|まいにち}の{小|ちい}さな{努力|どりょく}を{蓄積|ちくせき}することで、{大|おお}きな{成果|せいか}につながる。
examples.english: By accumulating small daily efforts, you can achieve great results.

notes:
A compound of {蓄|ちく} (store, save) and {積|せき} (pile up, accumulate). Can be used as a noun or as a suru verb ({蓄積|ちくせき}する).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- [thing]が{蓄積|ちくせき}する (something accumulates)
- [thing]を{蓄積|ちくせき}する (to accumulate something)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {疲労|ひろう}が{蓄積|ちくせき}する (fatigue accumulates)
- {知識|ちしき}を{蓄積|ちくせき}する (accumulate knowledge)
- データを{蓄積|ちくせき}する (accumulate data)
- {経験|けいけん}の{蓄積|ちくせき} (accumulation of experience)
- {脂肪|しぼう}の{蓄積|ちくせき} (fat buildup)

A versatile word used across many domains — health (fatigue, stress, fat), business (data, capital), and personal development (knowledge, experience). More formal than {溜|た}まる (to accumulate, informal).
